discovery_engine.mode_rule: Determine mode per topic/process, never globally for the whole company.
core_rules: A situation is not a friction.
A missing capability is not an opportunity unless it connects to a real upcoming intention or next step.
Not applicable today must never automatically mean no opportunity.
If the current way works well, close the friction branch.
Never recommend custom software directly from a situation or missing capability.
A mature company may have an emerging process; a young company may have a real operational friction.

qualification.policy: Use contextual qualification questions defined by topic. Never render a generic repeated 'Qu’est-ce qui vous gêne surtout?' block.
rules: Every follow-up must identify the specific information still missing.
Every follow-up must be capable of changing the analysis or branch.
Use concrete referents; avoid ça/cela/cette façon de faire when the referent is on a previous screen.
Consequence questions must offer a neutral exit such as 'Rien d’important pour le moment' when appropriate.
If current functioning is clearly healthy, close the branch.
Do not ask for a consequence if situation, friction and consequence are already sufficiently known.

opportunity_types.emerging_capability: Missing capability tied to real near-term intent.
opportunity_types.fit_gap: Existing solution/process does not sufficiently meet the current need.
opportunity_types.optimization: Current approach works reasonably well, but credible improvement desire and value evidence exist.
opportunity_types.healthy: Approach is appropriate and no meaningful improvement desire is supported.

optional_free_text.principle: Free text supplements structured answers and is never required for a useful result.

dimension_note.label_fr: Y a-t-il quelque chose d’important que les choix précédents ne vous ont pas permis d’exprimer?

final_note.label_fr: Y a-t-il autre chose que vous aimeriez préciser?
final_note.hint_fr: Une situation particulière, une façon de travailler ou un irritant que nous n’avons pas abordé.

rules: Only describe explored topics.
Never mention the questionnaire, diagnostic engine, or meeting in the analytical result.
Never jump directly from friction or missing capability to custom software.
Distinguish improvement opportunities from emerging capabilities.
For emerging capabilities, explain why the capability matters now based on the respondent's stated next step.
Do not present generic startup recommendations.
Allow healthy/no-opportunity results.
Never state a global low-opportunity conclusion unless minimum discovery coverage is met.
When coverage is partial, say only that the explored aspects appear to work well.
Never use a meeting or discussion as a caveat for incomplete analysis.
Do not include 'Ces pistes sont indicatives. Une discussion permet de les valider et de les prioriser.' or equivalent.
Use declared priority as the organizing thread of the result when at least one supported opportunity aligns with it.
State the declared priority near the beginning of the result without implying Cobreo has proven a solution.
Rank opportunities using both priority alignment and discovered operational value.
Do not suppress a strong off-priority opportunity.
Do not promote a weak opportunity solely because it matches declared priority.
When useful, explain whether an opportunity supports the declared priority directly or indirectly.
Healthy functioning must not automatically imply no optimization potential.
Optimization may be presented without describing the current process as problematic.
After adequate coverage and eligible optimization probes, a genuinely healthy result is valid.
Never imply everything in the business is good; healthy conclusions are limited to explored evidence.
Main recommendations require medium or high internal confidence.
Do not expose artificial numeric confidence percentages.

implementation_notes: V6.2 replaces symptom-first radars with neutral situation questions.
Do not end the diagnostic merely because two topics are currently not applicable.
Use near-term intent to decide whether a missing capability is irrelevant or emerging.
Never infer friction directly from a descriptive situation answer.
Determine existing_process vs emerging_capability per topic, not per company.
Progress is stage-based, never question-count-based.
Render explicit selection instructions for every multi-select with a limit.
Optional free text must remain optional and contextual.
Keep result analysis separate from lead-conversion UI.
Audit every single_select: keep it single only for mutually exclusive states or scales.
The operational scan is a discovery safety net, not a mandatory long questionnaire.
Ask frequency, effort and desire only when they can materially affect prioritization.
Tools are context until an observable limitation, handoff, cost or friction is confirmed.
Remove generic repeated consequence blocks and replace them with topic-specific follow-ups.
Do not globally conclude 'nothing to report' from narrow coverage.
Treat current_priority as explicit intent and persist it through result generation.
Do not close a branch because a website/tool/process exists; assess fit when relevant.
Product-information channels are multi-select.
All measurement questions require an explicit activity referent.
Display 'Tableurs (Excel, Google Sheets, etc.)' instead of bare 'Tableurs'.
Priority alignment affects exploration depth and ranking but never creates evidence.
V6.5 is the candidate for real-prospect testing; avoid further structural expansion until pilot observations justify it.
Whenever a relevant existing solution is detected and fit is unknown, ask a short contextual fit/satisfaction question.
Satisfaction means fit for the respondent's need or goal, not generic liking of the tool.
All frequency measurement copy must be authored/generated as a conjugated clause.
V6.6 adds optimization-without-pain as a first-class path.
Good fit closes friction discovery; eligible topics may receive one lightweight optimization probe.
Never repeat an optimization probe after an explicit no.
Main prospect recommendations require a supported evidence chain and medium/high internal confidence.
Never force an opportunity for conversion; a credible healthy result is valid.
Use the preproduction quality gate before broad client rollout.

rules: A capability's existence is not evidence that it meets the respondent's need.
When an existing capability is materially related to declared priority, consider a short contextual fit question.
Do not ask generic satisfaction questions across every tool/process.

measurement_model.policy: Measure only when the answer can change priority or confidence; do not ask every scale for every signal.
rules: Prefer behavioral scales over 1–10 ratings.
Do not fabricate time saved from ordinal answers.
High frequency plus moderate effort can justify an opportunity even if irritation is modest.
Respect low desire to improve.
rendering_rules: Every measurement instance must provide activity_label_fr and activity_label_lower_fr.
Never render a measurement question with an ambiguous pronoun whose referent exists only on a previous screen.
If a natural contextual sentence cannot be generated, do not ask the measurement.
Frequency questions must use a conjugated clause, e.g. 'À quelle fréquence suivez-vous...?'
Never render 'À quelle fréquence' followed directly by an infinitive.
Never render an ambiguous pronoun whose referent exists only on a previous screen.

copy_generation.rule: Do not concatenate 'À quelle fréquence' with an infinitive activity label. Each measurable activity must provide a conjugated frequency clause and natural effort/improvement labels.

coverage_model.principle: No global low-opportunity conclusion without sufficient breadth.
rules: Declared priority chooses the first deep branch but does not restrict later discovery.
If strong opportunities are found early, the scan may be shortened.
If no opportunities are found and coverage is low, broaden the scan before results.
If coverage remains low, result language must be limited to explored areas.

opportunity_scoring.rule: Combine available evidence qualitatively. Missing dimensions remain missing, not assumed.
guardrails: Declared priority alone cannot create an opportunity.
Existing capability alone cannot close an opportunity.
Fit-for-need evidence can strengthen or close a branch.
Strong discovered operational value may outrank direct priority alignment.

early_exit.rule: Offer early results only after sufficient coverage or multiple credible opportunities.

rules: Declared priority is a first-class intent signal.
It increases relevance and exploration depth but never proves a solution is needed.
Strong operational opportunities outside the declared priority may still rank highly.
Weak opportunities must not be promoted merely because they align with declared priority.
Use the declared priority to explain why a supported opportunity matters now.

priority_alignment.direct: Opportunity directly supports the declared priority.
priority_alignment.indirect: Opportunity may free capacity or reduce friction that supports the priority indirectly.
priority_alignment.none: Opportunity is valuable but not materially connected to the declared priority.

fit_model.principle: The existence of a site, tool, process, order method, document, workflow or system is context only. When that solution is relevant to an explored activity or declared priority, check whether it satisfies the current need before closing the branch.
rules: When a capability exists and is relevant to declared intent, measure whether it supports the intended outcome.
Prefer outcome-specific fit questions over generic satisfaction questions.
Do not ask satisfaction when it cannot change the analysis.
A tool or process may exist and still be a strong improvement opportunity.

ask_if: a solution exists and is directly related to the declared priority
a solution exists in a topic currently being explored
the answer could materially change opportunity ranking or branch closure
skip_if: the solution is incidental and unrelated to the explored need
fit has already been established in the same topic
the answer would not change analysis

fit_model.followup_rule: If fit is partial or poor, ask what the respondent would like the current solution to do better, using a contextual multi-select when possible. Do not jump to replacing the solution.

real_prospect_pilot.objective: Validate discovery quality, comprehension, relevance and abandonment risk with real prospects before another structural redesign.
real_prospect_pilot.recommended_sample: Use varied real prospects across size, maturity and sector; treat findings as qualitative until sample size and recruitment support stronger claims.

optimization_probe.principle: Good fit closes friction discovery, not automatically optimization discovery.

confidence.high: Multiple reinforcing signals directly support the recommendation.
confidence.medium: Credible opportunity with limited missing detail; use measured language.
confidence.low: Exploration hypothesis only; do not present as a main recommendation.

rules: Never invent missing evidence.
Priority alignment strengthens relevance but cannot replace evidence.
Working processes may still yield optimization opportunities when desire and value evidence exist.
Low-confidence ideas remain internal or explicitly exploratory.

preproduction_quality_gate.release_rule: Do not treat as broadly client-ready while any critical failure reproduces reliably.
preproduction_quality_gate.pilot_rule: After simulated gate passes, use a limited real-prospect pilot before wider release.
